evidence_summary: PubMed abstract reports two studies with 139 and 64 participants. Only nighttime sleep-related worry was consistently associated with sleep impairment.
Wiley journal abstract reports 507 undergraduates. Bedtime repetitive negative thinking moderated the stress-insomnia relationship, with differing subgroup patterns.
Systematic review: 12 articles included in synthesis, nine distinct insomnia models identified, and 20 cognitive factors extracted (39 including sub-factors).
Meta-analysis: 154 studies, 1,338 effect sizes, N=5,717. Sleep loss reduced positive affect and increased anxiety; negative-affect findings were mixed.
notes: Do not extend findings to claim that sleep loss directly causes nighttime overthinking.

evidence_summary: AASM guideline strongly recommends multicomponent CBT-I for chronic insomnia in adults. Sleep hygiene alone is not recommended as a standalone treatment.
Meta-analysis of 15 randomized trials: moderate-to-large effects on worry (g approximately -0.41 to -0.71), but small, non-reliable effects on rumination (g approximately -0.13).
notes: Use cautious language; evidence base is limited.
